page_hint: Chapter 3, §4 Measurement, bullet 3; also §5 Common Mistakes first bullet
quoted_clause: For MoE models, the number of experts × parameters-per-expert gives the total; the routing hyperparameter (top-k) × parameters-per-expert gives the active per token.
observed: This formula omits always-on attention/shared/embedding parameters. The chapter's own Mixtral example uses active = 2×5.7B routed experts + 1.4B always-on = 12.8B, not 11.4B.
correction: Change to 'top-k × parameters-per-expert gives the routed-expert active parameters; add always-on attention/shared/embedding parameters to get total active per token.' Also adjust Common Mistakes phrase 'only the routed experts are read' to include always-on parameters.
acceptance_test: Applying the corrected formula to the Mixtral example yields ~12.8B active, matching Table 3-2.
verdict_evidence: ch3:109 'top-k x parameters-per-expert gives the active per token' no always-on term; ch3:70 derives 12.8B = 11.4B routed + ~1.4B always-on.
fix_instruction: Amend to 'top-k x params-per-expert gives routed active; add always-on attention/shared/embedding for total active per token.'

observed: The right-hand side omits the FLOP unit; '25.6B' and '140B' can be read as parameters rather than FLOPs, although the intended values are 25.6 GFLOP and 140 GFLOP.
correction: Write '25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP' or '25.6B FLOP ÷ 140B FLOP'.
acceptance_test: The table derivation is dimensionally clear as FLOPs, not parameters.
verdict_evidence: ch3:198 (Table 3-3) '= 25.6B / 140B' no FLOP unit; Table 3-2 (ch3:74) writes '25.6 GFLOP / 140 GFLOP' for same derivation.
fix_instruction: Write '25.6 GFLOP ÷ 140 GFLOP' in Table 3-3, matching Table 3-2.

page_hint: Ch 3 §7 'What We Still Don't Know' — first bullet
quoted_clause: - **Exact active-fraction per token for commercial MoE models.** Model cards rarely publish the precise top-k routing distribution under real workloads. We know the architectural top-k (e.g., top-2 from 8 experts), but which experts are active varies with prompt content and token position; *the number* of active parameters per token is fixed by top-k and expert size under standard routing. Effective active count can vary only under variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert-unavailable fallback — an implementation-specific exception, not the default.
observed: The bullet is filed as an open question under [UNRESOLVED], but its own body resolves it: 'the number of active parameters per token is fixed by top-k and expert size under standard routing'. The genuinely open residue is narrow and implementation-specific (variable-k, capacity dropping, expert-unavailable fallback). As written, the section tells the reader that something is unknown when the chapter has in fact just settled it, which is the 'unknown because the manuscript has not yet done the work' category the book's own taxonomy is meant to exclude.
correction: Move the settled statement into §3 or §4 as a positive fact ('under standard top-k routing the active parameter count per token is deterministic: k x params-per-expert + always-on; only variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert-unavailable fallback make it vary'), and rewrite the §7 bullet as the narrow open question it actually is: 'Under which implementations do variable-k, capacity dropping, or expert-unavailable fallback actually fire, and how much do they move the effective active count?'
acceptance_test: Every bullet in a 'What We Still Don't Know' section states a question the chapter has not already answered; no bullet's own body contains its resolution.
verdict_evidence: ch03:164 titled 'Exact active-fraction per token' yet body settles it: fixed by top-k and expert size under standard routing; bullet resolves itself.
fix_instruction: Retitle to the residual question (how often variable-k / capacity dropping fires); move the deterministic k x params-per-expert line to ch03 section 3 or 4.

page_hint: Ch 3 §3 — subsection heading 'MoE model representative (Mixtral 8x7B class, [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION])' and its preamble; Table 3-2 caption
quoted_clause: We contrast with a representative MoE model in the Mixtral lineage. The exact parameter split is not always published in vendor model cards; the numbers below are plausibility-checked and flagged.
observed: Two problems. (a) The claim that the parameter split 'is not always published in vendor model cards' is misleading for the model actually being used: Mixtral 8x7B's total and active parameter counts are published by the model author (46.7B total, 12.9B active), and the book's numbers (47B / 12.8B) are within rounding of them. (b) The chapter labels the model [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] while simultaneously using a real named family's published geometry (32 layers, hidden 4096, GQA 8 x 128) for the KV comparison. A reader who knows Mixtral will read the numbers as Mixtral's actuals despite the label; a reader who does not will think the geometry is invented.
correction: Pick one of two honest framings. (i) Cite the model card: relabel the subsection '[1P][FACT] geometry, [canonical scenario][DERIVED] arithmetic' with the Mixtral model card as the source, and state the published 46.7B/12.9B figures alongside the book's rounded 47B/12.8B so the rounding is visible. (ii) Rename the model to a generic '8-expert MoE, 32L/4096H, GQA 8 x 128' and keep [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION], deleting the Mixtral attribution and the claim about unpublished splits. Do not keep the current mixture.
acceptance_test: The provenance label on the MoE geometry matches whether the geometry is a published fact or an invented variant; no sentence claims a parameter split is unpublished for a model whose split is published.
verdict_evidence: ch3:61 heading labels [ILLUSTRATIVE][ASSUMPTION] Mixtral 8x7B while ch3:196 reuses its real 32L/4096H GQA geometry; 'split not always published' inaccurate (46.7B/12.9B published).
fix_instruction: Ch3:61-74 — cite the Mixtral card (46.7B/12.9B) as [1P], or drop the Mixtral name and the unpublished-split sentence.

page_hint: Ch 3 §6 — 'Why the trend signal should not be read as "dense is dead"' and 'One verified 2026 transfer: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next'
quoted_clause: **Qwen3.8-27B** ([1P][FACT], source: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B) is a dense 27.8B model whose 4-bit weights fit on a single 24 GB consumer GPU, and **Muse Glimmer 30B** ([2°][FACT], source: Meta via vLLM-Recipes) is a dense 29.6B local-agentic model that runs in ~18 GB at ~5-bit weights.
observed: Two citation-hygiene problems in the same sentence. (a) 'source: HF Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B' is a bare model-card reference with no URL, unlike the inline links used elsewhere in the book; a reader cannot verify it from the page. (b) 'Muse Glimmer 30B' is attributed to 'Meta via vLLM-Recipes' and labelled [2°], but the underlying artifact is a first-party model card from the model's author; the house convention prefers primary sources where a primary source is readily available, and a recipe repository is a secondary restatement of a first-party claim. The [2°] label is honest but the sourcing choice is not the best available.
correction: Give both models inline links to their first-party model cards and label them [1P][FACT]; if a figure (e.g. the ~18 GB at ~5-bit figure) comes only from the recipe, split the claim: the parameter count and architecture from the model card [1P][FACT], the memory footprint from the recipe [2°][FACT], each labelled separately.
acceptance_test: Every model-specific factual claim in Ch 3 carries an inline link to a first-party artifact, and any figure that exists only in a secondary source is labelled [2°] on its own.
verdict_evidence: 'Muse Glimmer 30B' occurs exactly once (ch3:137) no URL/footnote/sources entry; Qwen3.8-27B HF link only elsewhere (ch7); claims unresolvable from page.
fix_instruction: Ch3:137 — add inline HF links for Qwen3.8-27B and Muse Glimmer 30B; tag the ~18 GB/5-bit figure [2°] separately.

observed: The MoE grid contains nine cells but only eight are labeled (E1-E8); the ninth cell (bottom-right) is blank white and is not represented in the legend. The legend defines exactly three swatches (blue = all 140 GB resident & active; gray = inactive experts; orange = active experts). A reader cannot tell whether the blank cell is the always-on/shared-weight block (3 GB), an empty slot, or a rendering artifact. Since the figure's headline claim is 'MoE total resident = 94 GB = 91 GB experts + 3 GB always-on', the always-on block is exactly the quantity the blank cell appears to stand for, and it is the one element left undecoded.
acceptance_test: Either label the ninth cell (e.g. 'shared/always-on 3 GB') and add a legend swatch for it, or remove it so the grid is 3x2 + a separate labeled always-on block. A reader must be able to account for all 94 GB from the drawn elements without doing arithmetic the figure does not show.
verdict_evidence: book p68: MoE grid 3x3 positions but only E1-E8 labelled; row-3/col-3 holds no box and no legend swatch decodes it; always-on exists only as text line '94 GB = 91 GB + 3 GB'.
fix_instruction: Draw the 8 experts as a 2x4 grid, or label/close the 9th slot, so every drawn cell maps to E1-E8; keep the 94=91+3 line as the always-on account.

observed: The 'noise prior' canvas does not read as noise. Its bars are of roughly the same varying heights as the 'clean continuous data' canvas, so the visual progression clean -> partly corrupted -> noise prior is carried entirely by the captions under the boxes rather than by the drawing. In a continuous diffusion the forward process drives the marginal toward a broad, near-uniform distribution; showing that flattening would make the corruption direction self-evident and would let the picture do the work the labels currently do.
acceptance_test: Make the third canvas visibly flatter (near-uniform bars) and, if desired, the second intermediate, so that a reader who ignores the labels still reads 'progressive corruption toward a prior'. Verify at print size that the flattening is visible.
verdict_evidence: book p53 lane A: 'noise prior' canvas keeps tall bars (1st/5th/8th) beside near-zero ones, spread comparable to 'clean continuous data'; no flattening toward uniform.
fix_instruction: Regenerate lane A so canvas 3 is near-uniform and canvas 2 intermediate; verify at print size that the flattening reads without the labels.

observed: Printed page 44 is a figure-only page whose figure begins roughly a quarter of the way down the page, leaving a large empty band at the top and a comparable band at the bottom. The page reads as an accidental float placement rather than a designed figure page. This is the same pattern visible on printed page 97 (FIG 6.1), suggesting a systematic float-placement issue rather than a one-off.
acceptance_test: Adjust float placement (or add a short lead-in paragraph) so the figure sits at the top of the page or the page is filled; no printed page should carry an unexplained blank band exceeding roughly 20% of the page height.
verdict_evidence: book p64: body ink starts 26.6% down (20.1% blank band under header), caption ends 72.0%, trailing blank 28%; other figure pages start 16.7-22.1%.
fix_instruction: Add a lead-in paragraph or retune the float so the printed-44 figure starts within 22% of the page top and the page is not 28% empty.

observed: The two-line annotation 'Denoising schedule progresses / Not two experts within one forward' is placed in the gap between the two dashed checkpoint-to-stage arrows, where it reads as a label on those arrows rather than as a statement about the stage-to-stage transition. The black arrow from 'High-noise stage' to 'Low-noise stage' already carries the schedule-progression meaning, so the annotation is both ambiguously placed and partly redundant.
acceptance_test: Move the annotation so it unambiguously annotates the horizontal stage-to-stage arrow (or place it as a caption-side note), and confirm at print size that no reader can take it as an arrow label for the dashed arrows.
verdict_evidence: book p64: two-line note 'Denoising schedule progresses / Not two experts within one forward' sits between the two dashed blue checkpoint->stage arrows and above the horizontal high->low arrow.
fix_instruction: Move the note below or beside the horizontal high-noise -> low-noise arrow, or into the caption, so it cannot read as a label on the dashed arrows.
